title: HostCapabilities
description: Canonical schema for host capabilities reported by Host Adapters. Strictly records factual availability and discrete options, forbidding automatic intelligence ranking or routing ranks.

host_id.description: Identifier of the agent host (e.g. codex, opencode, claude-code, generic).

adapter_id.description: Identifier of the adapter reporting these capabilities.

workspace.description: Canonical workspace directory inspected, if applicable.

observed_at.description: Timestamp when this host capability snapshot was observed.

platform.description: Optional OS/environment platform detail (e.g. darwin-arm64, linux-x64).

available_models.description: Factual inventory of models exposed by this host. Forbids routing_rank and intelligence assumptions.

supported_effort_values.description: Exact discrete string values supported by the host runtime for reasoning effort.

default_effort_value.description: Default reasoning effort value assumed by the host when none is specified.

capabilities.description: Execution and context capabilities supported by the host runtime.

model_info.description: Factual model descriptor. Exclusively describes presence and features without ranking or tier guessing.

id.description: Authentic model identifier as exposed by the host.

label.description: Human-readable model label provided by the host UI/runtime.

state.description: Availability state of this model on the host.

features.description: Technical features reported by the host (e.g. reasoning, tools, vision).

evidence_source.description: Provenance evidence verifying host capability or model presence.

locator.description: Path, CLI command, config key, or runtime API from which evidence was derived.

capability_entry.description: State of a specific host capability with supporting evidence.

model_selection_capability.description: Model selection capabilities and supported scopes.

concurrency_capability.description: Concurrent execution limits of the host runtime.

max_concurrency.description: Maximum parallel workers or subagents supported by the host pool.

configuration_mutation_capability.description: Whether the host supports programmatic configuration updates (file-based or live session).

supports_native_files.description: True if host configuration files (e.g. config.toml, settings.json) can be safely rendered and written.

supports_session_mutation.description: True if live session state can be altered via API or commands.
